description: Question bank on Indian Society and Its Dynamics - Major Social Problems (Chapter 5.4). Fully covers all points from the provided notes for KEA FDA/SDA examination preparation. Verify against current official sources before formal use.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is poverty?

options.A: A condition in which a person or household lacks sufficient resources to meet basic needs and participate adequately in society
options.B: A condition in which a person has no bank account
options.C: A condition in which a person lives in a city
options.D: A condition in which a person is unemployed for one day

questions.explanation: Poverty is a condition in which a person or household lacks sufficient resources to meet basic needs and to participate adequately in society. It may involve inadequate income or consumption as well as deprivation in health, education, housing, nutrition and living standards.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the two broad approaches to measuring poverty?

options.A: Income or consumption-based measurement and multidimensional measurement
options.B: Urban measurement and rural measurement
options.C: Census measurement and survey measurement
options.D: Direct measurement and indirect measurement

questions.explanation: The two broad approaches are income or consumption-based measurement and multidimensional measurement. Income or consumption measures assess resources available to a household, while multidimensional measures assess overlapping deprivations such as health, education and living standards.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is absolute poverty?

options.A: A condition in which people lack resources to meet a specified minimum standard of basic needs, using a defined poverty threshold
options.B: Having fewer resources than the median level in society
options.C: Poverty measured only through health indicators
options.D: Poverty found only in urban areas

questions.explanation: Absolute poverty refers to a condition in which people lack resources to meet a specified minimum standard of basic needs, using a defined poverty threshold.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is relative poverty?

options.A: Having substantially fewer resources than the typical or median level in a particular society, limiting ability to maintain socially accepted living standards and participate fully
options.B: Lacking resources to meet an absolute minimum threshold
options.C: Poverty measured only by income
options.D: Poverty that exists only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Relative poverty refers to having substantially fewer resources than the typical or median level in a particular society, limiting a person's ability to maintain socially accepted living standards and participate fully.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is multidimensional poverty?

options.A: Poverty measured through several dimensions of deprivation, commonly including health, education and standard of living
options.B: Poverty measured only through income
options.C: Poverty measured only through consumption
options.D: Poverty measured only through unemployment

questions.explanation: Multidimensional poverty is poverty measured through several dimensions of deprivation, commonly including health, education and standard of living, rather than income alone.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between absolute and relative poverty?

options.A: Absolute poverty is assessed against a defined minimum-needs threshold, whereas relative poverty is assessed in relation to the distribution of resources or living standards in a society
options.B: Absolute poverty is measured in cities, relative poverty in villages
options.C: Absolute poverty uses health indicators, relative poverty uses education indicators
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Absolute poverty is assessed against a defined minimum-needs threshold, whereas relative poverty is assessed in relation to the distribution of resources or living standards in a society.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes of poverty in India?

options.A: Unemployment and underemployment, low and insecure wages, unequal distribution of land and assets, low productivity, inadequate education and skills, social discrimination, ill health, indebtedness, regional disparities and vulnerability to shocks
options.B: Only unemployment
options.C: Only illiteracy
options.D: Only population growth

questions.explanation: Major causes include unemployment and underemployment, low and insecure wages, unequal distribution of land and assets, low productivity, inadequate education and skills, social discrimination, ill health, indebtedness, regional disparities and vulnerability to shocks.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the poverty trap?

options.A: A self-reinforcing situation in which low income restricts access to nutrition, healthcare, education, credit and productive assets, making it difficult to improve future income
options.B: A government scheme for poverty reduction
options.C: A method of measuring poverty
options.D: A type of unemployment

questions.explanation: A poverty trap is a self-reinforcing situation in which low income restricts access to nutrition, healthcare, education, credit and productive assets, making it difficult to improve future income.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is rural poverty?

options.A: Poverty experienced by people living in rural areas, often associated with landlessness, agricultural dependence, seasonal employment, low wages, indebtedness and inadequate access to services
options.B: Poverty found only among agricultural households
options.C: Poverty caused only by drought
options.D: Poverty measured only by land ownership

questions.explanation: Rural poverty is poverty experienced by people living in rural areas, often associated with landlessness, agricultural dependence, seasonal employment, low wages, indebtedness and inadequate access to services. Rural poverty is not limited to agricultural households.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is urban poverty?

options.A: Poverty experienced in towns and cities, involving insecure informal work, high housing costs, inadequate sanitation, overcrowding, limited social protection and uncertain access to essential services
options.B: Poverty found only in slums
options.C: Poverty caused only by migration
options.D: Poverty measured only by housing quality

questions.explanation: Urban poverty is poverty experienced in towns and cities and may involve insecure informal work, high housing costs, inadequate sanitation, overcrowding, limited social protection and uncertain access to essential services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the poverty line?

options.A: A threshold used to classify people or households as poor according to a specified method and reference period
options.B: A line drawn on a map showing poor districts
options.C: A legal minimum wage
options.D: A government scheme for the poor

questions.explanation: A poverty line is a threshold used to classify people or households as poor according to a specified method and reference period. The result depends on the methodology, prices, consumption basket and data used.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which committee is commonly associated with the Tendulkar methodology for estimating poverty in India?

options.A: The Expert Group chaired by Suresh D. Tendulkar, which submitted its report in 2009
options.B: The Expert Group chaired by C. Rangarajan
options.C: The Expert Group chaired by D. T. Lakdawala
options.D: The Expert Group chaired by Y. K. Alagh

questions.explanation: The Expert Group chaired by Suresh D. Tendulkar submitted its report in 2009 and proposed a revised methodology for estimating poverty in India.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which committee is associated with the Rangarajan poverty estimation methodology?

options.A: The Expert Group chaired by C. Rangarajan, which submitted its report in 2014
options.B: The Expert Group chaired by Suresh D. Tendulkar
options.C: The Expert Group chaired by D. T. Lakdawala
options.D: The Expert Group chaired by Y. K. Alagh

questions.explanation: The Expert Group chaired by C. Rangarajan submitted its report in 2014 and proposed a different poverty estimation methodology from the Tendulkar approach.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What was the purpose of the Lakdawala Expert Group?

options.A: It examined methodology for estimating poverty in India, and its recommendations were used in earlier official poverty estimates
options.B: It conducted the first census of India
options.C: It recommended the National Food Security Act
options.D: It established NITI Aayog

questions.explanation: The Expert Group chaired by D. T. Lakdawala examined methodology for estimating poverty in India and its recommendations were used in earlier official poverty estimates.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Multidimensional Poverty Index?

options.A: An index that identifies overlapping deprivations across indicators in areas such as health, education and living standards
options.B: An index that measures only income poverty
options.C: An index that measures unemployment only
options.D: An index that measures literacy only

questions.explanation: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) identifies overlapping deprivations across indicators in areas such as health, education and living standards. India's national MPI is developed by NITI Aayog using a national indicator framework.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which global organisations publish a global Multidimensional Poverty Index?

options.A: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) jointly
options.B: The World Bank and IMF
options.C: NITI Aayog and RBI
options.D: WHO and UNICEF

questions.explanation: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) jointly publish the global Multidimensional Poverty Index.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of NITI Aayog in multidimensional poverty measurement?

options.A: It has published national Multidimensional Poverty Index reports for India using indicators covering health, education and standard of living
options.B: It conducts the Census
options.C: It publishes the global MPI
options.D: It implements MGNREGA

questions.explanation: NITI Aayog has published national Multidimensional Poverty Index reports for India, using indicators covering health, education and standard of living to assess multiple deprivations.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005?

options.A: A rights-based rural employment law providing a legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work
options.B: A law providing subsidised foodgrains
options.C: A law providing pensions to the elderly
options.D: A law prohibiting child labour

questions.explanation: The MGNREGA is a rights-based rural employment law that provides a legal guarantee of up to 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the principal objective of MGNREGA?

options.A: To enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing guaranteed wage employment and creating durable community assets, while supporting inclusive and accountable local development
options.B: To provide free education to children
options.C: To distribute subsidised foodgrains
options.D: To provide pensions to widows

questions.explanation: Its objective is to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing guaranteed wage employment and creating durable community assets, while supporting inclusive and accountable local development.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Food Security Act, 2013?

options.A: A legal framework for food and nutritional security, including subsidised foodgrains to eligible persons under the Targeted Public Distribution System and nutritional entitlements for specified groups
options.B: A law guaranteeing rural wage employment
options.C: A law prohibiting dowry
options.D: A law regulating narcotic drugs

questions.explanation: The National Food Security Act, 2013, provides a legal framework for food and nutritional security, including subsidised foodgrains to eligible persons under the Targeted Public Distribution System and nutritional entitlements for specified groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Public Distribution System?

options.A: A government mechanism for distributing essential commodities, especially foodgrains, to eligible households through a network of fair price shops
options.B: A system of distributing free laptops
options.C: A system of providing rural employment
options.D: A system of providing legal aid

questions.explanation: The Public Distribution System (PDS) is a government mechanism for distributing essential commodities, especially foodgrains, to eligible households through a network of fair price shops. The Targeted PDS operates under the National Food Security Act and related rules.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Social Assistance Programme?

options.A: A centrally sponsored social assistance programme that includes pension and family-benefit components for eligible vulnerable groups, with implementation involving States and Union Territories
options.B: A rural employment guarantee programme
options.C: A food security programme
options.D: A skill development programme

questions.explanation: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a centrally sponsored social assistance programme that includes pension and family-benefit components for eligible vulnerable groups, with implementation involving States and Union Territories.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission?

options.A: A mission seeking to reduce rural poverty by organising poor rural households, especially women, into self-help groups and federations and supporting financial inclusion, livelihoods and access to services
options.B: A mission to provide urban housing
options.C: A mission to provide foodgrains
options.D: A mission to conduct the Census

questions.explanation: DAY-NRLM seeks to reduce rural poverty by organising poor rural households, especially women, into self-help groups and federations and supporting financial inclusion, livelihoods and access to services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major consequences of poverty?

options.A: Malnutrition, poor health, school dropout, child labour, inadequate housing, indebtedness, social exclusion, vulnerability to exploitation and restricted opportunities for social mobility
options.B: Only malnutrition
options.C: Only school dropout
options.D: Only indebtedness

questions.explanation: Consequences include malnutrition, poor health, school dropout, child labour, inadequate housing, indebtedness, social exclusion, vulnerability to exploitation and restricted opportunities for social mobility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can poverty be reduced?

options.A: Through productive employment, quality education, healthcare, nutrition, infrastructure, social protection, fair access to land and assets, financial inclusion, gender equality and effective implementation of welfare programmes
options.B: Only through free cash transfers
options.C: Only through population control
options.D: Only through foreign aid

questions.explanation: Poverty reduction requires productive employment, quality education, healthcare, nutrition, infrastructure, social protection, fair access to land and assets, financial inclusion, gender equality and effective implementation of welfare programmes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is unemployment?

options.A: A situation in which a person who is able and willing to work and is seeking or available for work does not have employment, according to the definition and reference period used by a labour-force survey
options.B: A situation in which a person works fewer hours than desired
options.C: A situation in which a person works below their skill level
options.D: A situation in which a person has no bank account

questions.explanation: Unemployment is a situation in which a person who is able and willing to work and is seeking or available for work does not have employment, according to the definition and reference period used by a labour-force survey. A person is generally classified as unemployed if the person is without work, is available for work and is seeking work or has taken steps to obtain work, subject to the survey's operational definition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the labour force?

options.A: People who are employed plus people who are unemployed and seeking or available for work under the relevant statistical definition
options.B: All people above 18 years of age
options.C: Only people who are employed
options.D: Only people who are unemployed

questions.explanation: The labour force consists of people who are employed plus people who are unemployed and seeking or available for work under the relevant statistical definition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the unemployment rate?

options.A: The percentage of unemployed persons in the labour force, calculated using the same population coverage and reference period
options.B: The percentage of unemployed persons in the total population
options.C: The number of unemployed persons in a district
options.D: The percentage of employed persons in the labour force

questions.explanation: The unemployment rate is the percentage of unemployed persons in the labour force, calculated using the same population coverage and reference period.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is disguised unemployment?

options.A: A situation in which more workers are engaged in an activity than are actually needed, so that removing some workers would not significantly reduce total output
options.B: A situation in which work is available only during particular seasons
options.C: A situation in which workers' skills do not match available jobs
options.D: A situation in which people are temporarily between jobs

questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment occurs when more workers are engaged in an activity than are actually needed, so that removing some workers would not significantly reduce total output. It is often discussed in relation to agriculture and family enterprises.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is seasonal unemployment?

options.A: Unemployment that occurs when work is available only during particular seasons or periods of the year, leaving workers without employment during the off-season
options.B: Unemployment caused by a downturn in overall economic activity
options.C: Unemployment while people move between jobs
options.D: Unemployment due to skill mismatch

questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment occurs when work is available only during particular seasons or periods of the year, leaving workers without employment during the off-season.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is structural unemployment?

options.A: Unemployment that occurs when the skills, location or qualifications of workers do not match the requirements or location of available jobs, often due to changes in technology or the economy
options.B: Unemployment that occurs when work is available only in particular seasons
options.C: Temporary unemployment while people move between jobs
options.D: Unemployment caused by a downturn in economic activity

questions.explanation: Structural unemployment occurs when the skills, location or qualifications of workers do not match the requirements or location of available jobs, often due to changes in technology or the economy.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is frictional unemployment?

options.A: Temporary unemployment that occurs while people move between jobs, enter the labour market or search for suitable employment
options.B: Unemployment due to a downturn in economic activity
options.C: Unemployment due to skill mismatch
options.D: Unemployment that occurs only in particular seasons

questions.explanation: Frictional unemployment is temporary unemployment that occurs while people move between jobs, enter the labour market or search for suitable employment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is cyclical unemployment?

options.A: Unemployment that results from a downturn in overall economic activity, when reduced demand for goods and services causes businesses to cut production and employment
options.B: Unemployment that occurs while people move between jobs
options.C: Unemployment due to skill mismatch
options.D: Unemployment that occurs only in particular seasons

questions.explanation: Cyclical unemployment results from a downturn in overall economic activity, when reduced demand for goods and services causes businesses to cut production and employment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is educated unemployment?

options.A: A situation in which people with formal educational qualifications are unable to obtain suitable employment, possibly reflecting insufficient job creation, skill mismatch, location constraints or unrealistic expectations
options.B: Unemployment among people who have never attended school
options.C: Unemployment caused by a downturn in economic activity
options.D: Unemployment that occurs only in particular seasons

questions.explanation: Educated unemployment occurs when people with formal educational qualifications are unable to obtain suitable employment. It may reflect insufficient job creation, skill mismatch, location constraints or unrealistic expectations about available work.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is underemployment?

options.A: A situation in which a person works fewer hours than desired, works below their skill or qualification level, or is engaged in work that does not fully utilise their productive capacity
options.B: A situation in which a person has no work but is actively seeking employment
options.C: A situation in which a person is temporarily between jobs
options.D: A situation in which a person is unemployed due to a downturn

questions.explanation: Underemployment occurs when a person works fewer hours than desired, works below their skill or qualification level, or is engaged in work that does not fully utilise their productive capacity.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is open unemployment?

options.A: A situation in which people have no work but are actively seeking or available for employment, as defined by the relevant survey
options.B: A situation in which people work fewer hours than desired
options.C: A situation in which people work below their skill level
options.D: A situation in which people are engaged in work that does not fully utilise their capacity

questions.explanation: Open unemployment refers to people who have no work but are actively seeking or available for employment, as defined by the relevant survey.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between unemployment and underemployment?

options.A: Unemployment means a person has no employment under the applicable statistical definition, whereas underemployment means the person has some work but the hours, income or use of skills are inadequate
options.B: Unemployment applies only to rural areas, underemployment only to urban areas
options.C: Unemployment is temporary, underemployment is permanent
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Unemployment means a person has no employment under the applicable statistical definition. Underemployment means the person has some work but the hours, income or use of skills are inadequate.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Periodic Labour Force Survey?

options.A: A survey conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation to provide estimates of employment, unemployment and labour-force participation
options.B: A survey conducted by NITI Aayog to measure poverty
options.C: A survey conducted by the RBI to measure inflation
options.D: A survey conducted by the Census Commissioner to count population

questions.explanation: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation to provide estimates of employment, unemployment and labour-force participation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which organisation conducts the Periodic Labour Force Survey?

options.A: The National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
options.B: NITI Aayog
options.C: The Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner

questions.explanation: The National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, conducts the PLFS.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the usual status approach in labour-force measurement?

options.A: An approach that classifies a person's activity based on a longer reference period, generally the preceding 365 days, identifying principal and subsidiary economic activity according to survey rules
options.B: An approach that classifies activity based on the seven days preceding the survey
options.C: An approach that measures only unemployment rate
options.D: An approach that measures only literacy

questions.explanation: Usual status classifies a person's activity based on a longer reference period, generally the preceding 365 days, and identifies principal and subsidiary economic activity according to survey rules.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the current weekly status approach?

options.A: An approach that classifies a person's activity based on the seven days preceding the survey, according to specified time and activity criteria
options.B: An approach that classifies activity based on the preceding 365 days
options.C: An approach that measures only underemployment
options.D: An approach that measures only labour-force participation rate

questions.explanation: Current weekly status classifies a person's activity based on the seven days preceding the survey, according to specified time and activity criteria.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana?

options.A: A skill-development scheme intended to support skill training, certification and employability
options.B: A rural employment guarantee scheme
options.C: A food security scheme
options.D: A pension scheme

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is a skill-development scheme intended to support skill training, certification and employability. Its components and current implementation guidelines should be checked in the latest official releases.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Career Service?

options.A: A Ministry of Labour and Employment initiative that provides career-related services such as job search, job matching, career counselling and information through its portal and associated services
options.B: A scheme providing free foodgrains
options.C: A scheme providing rural wage employment
options.D: A scheme providing pensions to the elderly

questions.explanation: The National Career Service is a Ministry of Labour and Employment initiative that provides career-related services such as job search, job matching, career counselling and information through its portal and associated services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between labour-force participation rate and worker population ratio?

options.A: The labour-force participation rate is the percentage of the population that is employed or unemployed and seeking or available for work, while the worker population ratio is the percentage of the population that is employed
options.B: The labour-force participation rate measures only employment, while the worker population ratio measures only unemployment
options.C: Both measure the same thing
options.D: The labour-force participation rate applies only to rural areas, the worker population ratio only to urban areas

questions.explanation: The labour-force participation rate is the percentage of the population that is employed or unemployed and seeking or available for work. The worker population ratio is the percentage of the population that is employed.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can unemployment be reduced?

options.A: Through labour-intensive industrial growth, quality education, vocational training, apprenticeships, support for micro and small enterprises, infrastructure investment, women's workforce participation, career services and better alignment of skills with labour demand
options.B: Only through population control
options.C: Only through foreign investment
options.D: Only through free cash transfers

questions.explanation: Measures include labour-intensive industrial growth, quality education, vocational training, apprenticeships, support for micro and small enterprises, infrastructure investment, women's workforce participation, career services and better alignment of skills with labour demand.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is literacy?

options.A: The ability to read and write with understanding in a language, as defined by the statistical framework used for measurement
options.B: The ability to speak a language fluently
options.C: The ability to use a computer
options.D: The ability to solve mathematical problems only

questions.explanation: Literacy is the ability to read and write with understanding in a language, as defined by the statistical framework used for measurement.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is illiteracy?

options.A: The inability to read and write with understanding in any language under the relevant statistical definition
options.B: The inability to speak a language
options.C: The inability to use a computer
options.D: The inability to solve mathematical problems

questions.explanation: Illiteracy is the inability to read and write with understanding in any language under the relevant statistical definition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What literacy definition has traditionally been used by the Census of India?

options.A: A person aged seven years or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate; a person who can only read but cannot write is not treated as literate
options.B: A person aged five years or above who can read is treated as literate
options.C: A person aged ten years or above who can sign their name is treated as literate
options.D: A person aged fifteen years or above who can read and write English is treated as literate

questions.explanation: For Census purposes, a person aged seven years or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate. A person who can only read but cannot write is not treated as literate under this definition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between literacy and education?

options.A: Literacy is a basic ability to read and write with understanding, while education is a broader process that includes knowledge, skills, values, reasoning, attitudes and learning
options.B: Literacy is broader than education
options.C: Literacy and education are identical
options.D: Literacy applies only to adults, education only to children

questions.explanation: Literacy is a basic ability to read and write with understanding. Education is a broader process that includes knowledge, skills, values, reasoning, attitudes and learning.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is functional literacy?

options.A: The ability to use reading, writing and numeracy skills to manage everyday tasks and participate effectively in social, economic and civic life
options.B: The ability to read and write only one's own name
options.C: The ability to read classical literature
options.D: The ability to teach literacy to others

questions.explanation: Functional literacy is the ability to use reading, writing and numeracy skills to manage everyday tasks and participate effectively in social, economic and civic life.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is adult literacy?

options.A: Programmes and learning opportunities that help adults acquire or improve reading, writing, numeracy and related life skills
options.B: Literacy programmes for children below 14 years
options.C: Literacy programmes for senior citizens only
options.D: Literacy programmes conducted only in schools

questions.explanation: Adult literacy refers to programmes and learning opportunities that help adults acquire or improve reading, writing, numeracy and related life skills.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes of illiteracy?

options.A: Poverty, lack of nearby schools, inadequate school infrastructure, child labour, gender discrimination, disability-related barriers, language barriers, conflict, migration, poor learning quality and social exclusion
options.B: Only poverty
options.C: Only lack of schools
options.D: Only gender discrimination

questions.explanation: Causes include poverty, lack of nearby schools, inadequate school infrastructure, child labour, gender discrimination, disability-related barriers, language barriers, conflict, migration, poor learning quality and social exclusion.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the consequences of illiteracy?

options.A: It can limit access to employment, public services, health information, legal rights, financial services, digital tools and political participation, and can reinforce intergenerational poverty
options.B: It has no effect on employment
options.C: It only affects political participation
options.D: It only affects access to digital tools

questions.explanation: Illiteracy can limit access to employment, public services, health information, legal rights, financial services, digital tools and political participation. It can also reinforce intergenerational poverty.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution provides free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years?

options.A: Article 21A
options.B: Article 45
options.C: Article 51A(k)
options.D: Article 46

questions.explanation: Article 21A provides free and compulsory education to all children aged six to fourteen years in the manner determined by law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 21A?

options.A: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002
options.B: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976
options.C: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
options.D: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016

questions.explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, inserted Article 21A and made related changes to the constitutional framework for education.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which law gives effect to the right to education under Article 21A?

options.A: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, commonly called the RTE Act, which came into force on 1 April 2010
options.B: The National Food Security Act, 2013
options.C: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
options.D: The Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986

questions.explanation: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, commonly called the RTE Act, came into force on 1 April 2010.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 45 provide?

options.A: It directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years
options.B: It provides free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
options.C: It makes it a fundamental duty of parents to provide education to children
options.D: It abolishes untouchability

questions.explanation: Article 45 directs the State to endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What does Article 51A(k) provide?

options.A: It makes it a fundamental duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years
options.B: It provides free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years
options.C: It directs the State to provide early childhood care and education
options.D: It prohibits employment of children below 14 years in hazardous work

questions.explanation: Article 51A(k) makes it a fundamental duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Literacy Mission?

options.A: A mission launched in 1988 to promote adult literacy, with emphasis on functional literacy and the participation of non-literate adults
options.B: A mission launched in 2009 with focus on female literacy
options.C: A mission launched in 2022 for non-literate persons aged 15 and above
options.D: A mission launched in 2015 to promote girl child education

questions.explanation: The National Literacy Mission was launched in 1988 to promote adult literacy, with emphasis on functional literacy and the participation of non-literate adults. Its programmes evolved over time.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is Saakshar Bharat?

options.A: A centrally sponsored adult education programme launched in 2009, with a focus on female literacy and adult education in eligible districts
options.B: A programme launched in 1988 for adult literacy
options.C: A programme launched in 2022 for non-literate persons aged 15 and above
options.D: A programme launched in 2015 for girl child education

questions.explanation: Saakshar Bharat was a centrally sponsored adult education programme launched in 2009, with a focus on female literacy and adult education in eligible districts. It is a historical programme and should not be confused with current schemes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the New India Literacy Programme?

options.A: A centrally sponsored scheme for the period 2022-23 to 2026-27, aimed at promoting education for non-literate persons aged 15 years and above, with components including foundational literacy and numeracy, critical life skills and continuing education
options.B: A programme launched in 1988 for adult literacy
options.C: A programme launched in 2009 with focus on female literacy
options.D: A programme launched in 2015 for girl child education

questions.explanation: The New India Literacy Programme, also known as ULLAS, is a centrally sponsored scheme for the period 2022-23 to 2026-27, aimed at promoting education for non-literate persons aged 15 years and above, with components including foundational literacy and numeracy, critical life skills and continuing education.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is Samagra Shiksha?

options.A: An integrated centrally sponsored school education programme covering the continuum from pre-school to Class XII, supporting access, equity, quality, teacher education and related school reforms
options.B: An adult literacy programme
options.C: A rural employment programme
options.D: A food security programme

questions.explanation: Samagra Shiksha is an integrated centrally sponsored school education programme covering the continuum from pre-school to Class XII, supporting access, equity, quality, teacher education and related school reforms.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the purpose of the National Education Policy 2020 in relation to literacy?

options.A: It places strong emphasis on foundational literacy and numeracy, early childhood care and education, equitable access and improving learning outcomes
options.B: It focuses only on higher education
options.C: It focuses only on adult literacy
options.D: It focuses only on vocational training

questions.explanation: NEP 2020 places strong emphasis on foundational literacy and numeracy, early childhood care and education, equitable access and improving learning outcomes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can illiteracy be reduced?

options.A: Through universal school access, quality teaching, adult education, local-language learning support, gender-sensitive facilities, inclusive education, financial support and community participation
options.B: Only through adult education
options.C: Only through building more schools
options.D: Only through financial support

questions.explanation: Illiteracy can be reduced through universal school access, quality teaching, adult education, local-language learning support, gender-sensitive facilities, inclusive education, financial support and community participation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is population growth?

options.A: The increase in the number of people living in a specified area over a specified period
options.B: The number of people living per square kilometre
options.C: The distribution of population across age groups
options.D: The movement of people from one place to another

questions.explanation: Population growth is the increase in the number of people living in a specified area over a specified period.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the population growth rate?

options.A: The percentage change in population over a given period, resulting from births, deaths and migration
options.B: The number of live births per 1,000 people
options.C: The number of deaths per 1,000 people
options.D: The number of people per square kilometre

questions.explanation: The population growth rate measures the percentage change in population over a given period, resulting from births, deaths and migration.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major components of population change?

options.A: Fertility or births, mortality or deaths, and migration into or out of the area
options.B: Only births and deaths
options.C: Only migration
options.D: Only fertility and migration

questions.explanation: The three major components are fertility or births, mortality or deaths, and migration into or out of the area.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the birth rate?

options.A: The number of live births in a year per 1,000 people in the mid-year population
options.B: The number of deaths in a year per 1,000 people
options.C: The average number of children a woman would have over her lifetime
options.D: The number of people per square kilometre

questions.explanation: The crude birth rate is the number of live births in a year per 1,000 people in the mid-year population.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the death rate?

options.A: The number of deaths in a year per 1,000 people in the mid-year population
options.B: The number of live births in a year per 1,000 people
options.C: The number of deaths of children below one year per 1,000 live births
options.D: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births

questions.explanation: The crude death rate is the number of deaths in a year per 1,000 people in the mid-year population.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the fertility rate?

options.A: The total fertility rate estimates the average number of children a woman would have over her lifetime if she experienced the age-specific fertility rates of a particular period
options.B: The number of live births in a year per 1,000 people
options.C: The number of deaths in a year per 1,000 people
options.D: The number of people per square kilometre

questions.explanation: The total fertility rate estimates the average number of children a woman would have over her lifetime if she experienced the age-specific fertility rates of a particular period.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is replacement-level fertility?

options.A: The level of fertility at which a generation of women would, on average, have enough daughters to replace themselves in the population, in the absence of migration; a commonly used approximate benchmark for many low-mortality populations is about 2.1 births per woman
options.B: The level of fertility at which population stops growing entirely
options.C: The level of fertility at which birth rate equals death rate
options.D: The level of fertility at which every woman has exactly two children

questions.explanation: Replacement-level fertility is the level of fertility at which a generation of women would, on average, have enough daughters to replace themselves in the population, in the absence of migration. A commonly used approximate benchmark for many low-mortality populations is about 2.1 births per woman, but the exact level varies.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is infant mortality rate?

options.A: The number of deaths of children below one year of age per 1,000 live births in a specified period
options.B: The number of deaths of children below five years of age per 1,000 live births
options.C: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
options.D: The number of deaths in a year per 1,000 people

questions.explanation: The infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of children below one year of age per 1,000 live births in a specified period.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is maternal mortality ratio?

options.A: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births during a specified period, according to the applicable definition
options.B: The number of deaths of children below one year per 1,000 live births
options.C: The number of deaths in a year per 1,000 people
options.D: The number of live births in a year per 1,000 people

questions.explanation: The maternal mortality ratio is the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births during a specified period, according to the applicable definition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is population density?

options.A: The number of people living per unit of land area, commonly expressed as persons per square kilometre
options.B: The percentage change in population over a given period
options.C: The distribution of population across age groups
options.D: The movement of people from one place to another

questions.explanation: Population density is the number of people living per unit of land area, commonly expressed as persons per square kilometre.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the commonly described stages of demographic transition?

options.A: A simplified model describes four stages: high stationary, early expanding, late expanding and low stationary; some versions include a fifth stage to discuss population decline or very low fertility
options.B: Three stages: high, medium and low
options.C: Two stages: growth and decline
options.D: Five stages: birth, death, migration, growth and decline

questions.explanation: A simplified model describes four stages: high stationary, early expanding, late expanding and low stationary. Some versions include a fifth stage to discuss population decline or very low fertility.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is population explosion?

options.A: A rapid increase in population over a relatively short period, often when mortality declines while fertility remains high
options.B: A gradual increase in population over centuries
options.C: A decrease in population due to high mortality
options.D: The movement of people from one country to another

questions.explanation: Population explosion refers to a rapid increase in population over a relatively short period, often when mortality declines while fertility remains high.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the age structure of a population?

options.A: The distribution of a population across age groups, such as children, working-age adults and older persons
options.B: The number of people per square kilometre
options.C: The percentage change in population over a given period
options.D: The movement of people from one place to another

questions.explanation: Age structure is the distribution of a population across age groups, such as children, working-age adults and older persons.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the dependency ratio?

options.A: A ratio comparing the population commonly considered dependent, such as children and older persons, with the working-age population, with exact age boundaries depending on the statistical definition
options.B: The ratio of births to deaths in a year
options.C: The ratio of males to females in a population
options.D: The ratio of urban to rural population

questions.explanation: The dependency ratio compares the population commonly considered dependent, such as children and older persons, with the working-age population. The exact age boundaries used depend on the statistical definition.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a demographic dividend?

options.A: The potential economic benefit that can arise when the share of working-age people becomes relatively large compared with dependants, provided that education, health, skills and employment opportunities are adequate
options.B: The economic cost of an ageing population
options.C: The financial assistance provided to families with children
options.D: The increase in population due to migration

questions.explanation: A demographic dividend is the potential economic benefit that can arise when the share of working-age people becomes relatively large compared with dependants, provided that education, health, skills and employment opportunities are adequate.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is population ageing?

options.A: An increase in the proportion of older persons in the population, often associated with lower fertility and longer life expectancy
options.B: An increase in the proportion of children in the population
options.C: A decrease in the working-age population due to migration
options.D: A rapid increase in population over a short period

questions.explanation: Population ageing is an increase in the proportion of older persons in the population, often associated with lower fertility and longer life expectancy.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is migration in population studies?

options.A: The movement of people from one usual place of residence to another, either within a country or across national borders
options.B: The increase in the number of people in a specified area
options.C: The distribution of population across age groups
options.D: The number of people per square kilometre

questions.explanation: Migration is the movement of people from one usual place of residence to another, either within a country or across national borders.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Population Policy 2000?

options.A: A framework for stabilising population and improving reproductive and child health, with immediate, medium-term and long-term objectives, and a long-term objective to achieve a stable population consistent with sustainable development
options.B: A law prohibiting child marriage
options.C: A scheme providing free education to children
options.D: A programme for adult literacy

questions.explanation: The National Population Policy 2000 provides a framework for stabilising population and improving reproductive and child health, with immediate, medium-term and long-term objectives. Its long-term objective was to achieve a stable population consistent with sustainable development.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the National Family Health Survey?

options.A: A large-scale, nationally representative household survey that provides data on population, health, nutrition, fertility, family planning and related indicators
options.B: A survey conducted by the RBI on inflation
options.C: A survey conducted by NITI Aayog on poverty
options.D: A survey conducted by the Election Commission on voters

questions.explanation: The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) is a large-scale, nationally representative household survey that provides data on population, health, nutrition, fertility, family planning and related indicators.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which organisation coordinates the National Family Health Survey?

options.A: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with the International Institute for Population Sciences serving as the nodal agency for its implementation
options.B: NITI Aayog
options.C: The Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare coordinates the NFHS, with the International Institute for Population Sciences serving as the nodal agency for its implementation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the Sample Registration System?

options.A: A system operated by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, that provides estimates of fertility and mortality indicators through a dual-record system
options.B: A system conducted by NITI Aayog to measure poverty
options.C: A system conducted by the RBI to measure inflation
options.D: A system conducted by the Election Commission to register voters

questions.explanation: The Sample Registration System (SRS), operated by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, provides estimates of fertility and mortality indicators through a dual-record system.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional provision deals with census?

options.A: Article 246 read with the Seventh Schedule places 'Census' in Entry 69 of the Union List, giving Parliament legislative competence over census matters
options.B: Article 21A
options.C: Article 338
options.D: Article 280

questions.explanation: Article 246 read with the Seventh Schedule places 'Census' in Entry 69 of the Union List, giving Parliament legislative competence over census matters.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can population growth be addressed through rights-based policy?

options.A: Through policies that support voluntary family planning, reproductive healthcare, girls' education, women's empowerment, child survival, access to contraception and informed decision-making without coercion or discrimination
options.B: Only through coercive population control measures
options.C: Only through incentives for having fewer children
options.D: Only through restrictions on marriage

questions.explanation: Policies can support voluntary family planning, reproductive healthcare, girls' education, women's empowerment, child survival, access to contraception and informed decision-making without coercion or discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Is population growth always a social problem?

options.A: No; population growth can expand the workforce and market, but its effects depend on resources, productivity, public services, environmental sustainability, age structure and the availability of decent employment
options.B: Yes, it is always a social problem
options.C: Yes, because it always leads to poverty
options.D: No, because it never has any negative effects

questions.explanation: No. Population growth can expand the workforce and market, but its effects depend on resources, productivity, public services, environmental sustainability, age structure and the availability of decent employment.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is caste discrimination?

options.A: Unequal or degrading treatment of a person because of caste identity or perceived caste status, including exclusion, denial of opportunities, segregation, humiliation or violence
options.B: Unequal treatment based on economic class only
options.C: Unequal treatment based on gender only
options.D: Unequal treatment based on religion only

questions.explanation: Caste discrimination is unequal or degrading treatment of a person because of caste identity or perceived caste status, including exclusion, denial of opportunities, segregation, humiliation or violence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is untouchability?

options.A: A historically practised system of social exclusion and discrimination against certain communities; Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form
options.B: A system of providing free education to certain communities
options.C: A system of reservation in public employment
options.D: A system of land distribution to certain communities

questions.explanation: Untouchability is a historically practised system of social exclusion and discrimination against certain communities. Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?

options.A: Article 17
options.B: Article 15
options.C: Article 16
options.D: Article 46

questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article prohibits discrimination on grounds including caste?

options.A: Article 15
options.B: Article 17
options.C: Article 16
options.D: Article 46

questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits the State from discriminating against citizens on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, subject to the Constitution's provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment?

options.A: Article 16
options.B: Article 15
options.C: Article 17
options.D: Article 46

questions.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits specified forms of discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections?

options.A: Article 46
options.B: Article 15
options.C: Article 16
options.D: Article 17

questions.explanation: Article 46 directs the State to promote the educational and economic interests of weaker sections, particularly Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and protect them from social injustice and exploitation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Act punishes the enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability?

options.A: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.B: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.C: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
options.D: The National Food Security Act, 2013

questions.explanation: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, provides penalties for the enforcement of disabilities arising from untouchability.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Act addresses atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
options.B: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
options.C: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
options.D: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956

questions.explanation: The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, specifies offences and provides for special courts, relief and rehabilitation measures and other safeguards.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional Article provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Article 338
options.B: Article 338A
options.C: Article 338B
options.D: Article 341

questions.explanation: Article 338 provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional Article provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 338A
options.B: Article 338
options.C: Article 338B
options.D: Article 342

questions.explanation: Article 338A provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which constitutional Article provides for the National Commission for Backward Classes?

options.A: Article 338B
options.B: Article 338
options.C: Article 338A
options.D: Article 341

questions.explanation: Article 338B provides for the National Commission for Backward Classes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article empowers the President to specify Scheduled Castes?

options.A: Article 341
options.B: Article 342
options.C: Article 338
options.D: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 341 empowers the President to specify Scheduled Castes in relation to a State or Union Territory, with Parliament empowered to include or exclude groups by law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article empowers the President to specify Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: Article 342
options.B: Article 341
options.C: Article 338
options.D: Article 338A

questions.explanation: Article 342 empowers the President to specify Scheduled Tribes in relation to a State or Union Territory, with Parliament empowered to include or exclude groups by law.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is casteism?

options.A: Excessive loyalty to one's caste combined with prejudice, discrimination or hostility towards other caste groups
options.B: A system of reservation in education
options.C: A system of land distribution
options.D: A system of adult literacy

questions.explanation: Casteism is excessive loyalty to one's caste combined with prejudice, discrimination or hostility towards other caste groups.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are common forms of caste discrimination?

options.A: Exclusion from public spaces or services, discriminatory treatment in education and employment, segregation, denial of access to resources, caste-based insults, social boycott, forced or degrading labour and violence
options.B: Only exclusion from public spaces
options.C: Only discriminatory treatment in education
options.D: Only caste-based insults

questions.explanation: Forms include exclusion from public spaces or services, discriminatory treatment in education and employment, segregation, denial of access to resources, caste-based insults, social boycott, forced or degrading labour and violence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the purpose of reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?

options.A: It is an affirmative-action measure intended to improve representation and access to education, public employment and elected institutions for historically disadvantaged groups under relevant constitutional provisions and laws
options.B: It is a measure to reduce population growth
options.C: It is a measure to promote adult literacy
options.D: It is a measure to provide food security

questions.explanation: Reservation is an affirmative-action measure intended to improve representation and access to education, public employment and elected institutions for historically disadvantaged groups under relevant constitutional provisions and laws.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between caste and class discrimination?

options.A: Caste discrimination is based on caste identity or perceived caste status, while class discrimination is based on economic or social class position; the two can overlap but are not identical
options.B: Caste discrimination is based on economic position, while class discrimination is based on caste identity
options.C: Both are based on religion only
options.D: Both are based on gender only

questions.explanation: Caste discrimination is based on caste identity or perceived caste status. Class discrimination is based on economic or social class position. The two can overlap but are not identical.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can caste discrimination be reduced?

options.A: Through enforcement of anti-discrimination laws, quality education, economic opportunity, social awareness, representation, access to justice, protection of victims and accountability for discriminatory practices
options.B: Only through reservation
options.C: Only through education
options.D: Only through legal enforcement

questions.explanation: Measures include enforcement of anti-discrimination laws, quality education, economic opportunity, social awareness, representation, access to justice, protection of victims and accountability for discriminatory practices.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is gender inequality?

options.A: The unequal distribution of rights, opportunities, resources, responsibilities, power and social status among people because of gender
options.B: The unequal distribution of resources based on caste only
options.C: The unequal distribution of resources based on religion only
options.D: The unequal distribution of resources based on region only

questions.explanation: Gender inequality is the unequal distribution of rights, opportunities, resources, responsibilities, power and social status among people because of gender.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between sex and gender?

options.A: Sex generally refers to biological attributes used in classification, while gender refers to socially shaped roles, expectations, identities and relations; the terms are related but not interchangeable
options.B: Sex refers to social roles, while gender refers to biological attributes
options.C: Sex and gender are identical terms
options.D: Sex applies only to humans, gender only to animals

questions.explanation: Sex generally refers to biological attributes used in classification, while gender refers to socially shaped roles, expectations, identities and relations. The terms are related but not interchangeable.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is patriarchy?

options.A: A social system in which men, particularly senior men, hold disproportionate power and authority in family, economic, political and social institutions
options.B: A social system in which women hold disproportionate power
options.C: A system of equal power between men and women
options.D: A system of government by the elderly

questions.explanation: Patriarchy is a social system in which men, particularly senior men, hold disproportionate power and authority in family, economic, political and social institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is gender stereotyping?

options.A: Assigning fixed characteristics, abilities or roles to people on the basis of gender, such as assuming that particular occupations or domestic duties belong only to women or men
options.B: Assigning fixed characteristics based on caste
options.C: Assigning fixed characteristics based on religion
options.D: Assigning fixed characteristics based on age

questions.explanation: Gender stereotyping is assigning fixed characteristics, abilities or roles to people on the basis of gender, such as assuming that particular occupations or domestic duties belong only to women or men.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are major indicators of gender inequality?

options.A: Differences in literacy, school participation, nutrition, health, wages, workforce participation, political representation, property ownership, unpaid care work, safety and access to decision-making
options.B: Only differences in literacy
options.C: Only differences in wages
options.D: Only differences in political representation

questions.explanation: Indicators include differences in literacy, school participation, nutrition, health, wages, workforce participation, political representation, property ownership, unpaid care work, safety and access to decision-making.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes of gender inequality in India?

options.A: Patriarchal norms, son preference, unequal care responsibilities, discrimination in education and employment, violence, unequal access to property and resources, early marriage and restrictive social expectations
options.B: Only patriarchal norms
options.C: Only son preference
options.D: Only unequal access to property

questions.explanation: Causes include patriarchal norms, son preference, unequal care responsibilities, discrimination in education and employment, violence, unequal access to property and resources, early marriage and restrictive social expectations.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the gender pay gap?

options.A: The difference between the average earnings of women and men, commonly expressed as a percentage of men's earnings, which can reflect occupational segregation, unequal hours, discrimination and differences in seniority or work conditions
options.B: The difference between the number of men and women in employment
options.C: The difference between male and female literacy rates
options.D: The difference between male and female life expectancy

questions.explanation: The gender pay gap is the difference between the average earnings of women and men, commonly expressed as a percentage of men's earnings. It can reflect occupational segregation, unequal hours, discrimination and differences in seniority or work conditions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the unpaid care burden?

options.A: Unpaid household and caregiving work, such as cooking, cleaning, childcare and elder care, which is disproportionately performed by women in many societies
options.B: The burden of paying taxes
options.C: The burden of agricultural work
options.D: The burden of industrial work

questions.explanation: The unpaid care burden refers to unpaid household and caregiving work, such as cooking, cleaning, childcare and elder care, which is disproportionately performed by women in many societies.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article guarantees equality before the law?

options.A: Article 14
options.B: Article 15
options.C: Article 16
options.D: Article 21A

questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person within the territory of India.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article prohibits discrimination on grounds of sex?

options.A: Article 15
options.B: Article 14
options.C: Article 16
options.D: Article 39(d)

questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits the State from discriminating against citizens on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article permits special provisions for women and children?

options.A: Article 15(3)
options.B: Article 15(1)
options.C: Article 16
options.D: Article 42

questions.explanation: Article 15(3) allows the State to make special provisions for women and children.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article provides equality of opportunity in public employment?

options.A: Article 16
options.B: Article 14
options.C: Article 15
options.D: Article 39(d)

questions.explanation: Article 16 provides equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits specified forms of discrimination.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Directive Principle provides for equal pay for equal work?

options.A: Article 39(d)
options.B: Article 42
options.C: Article 46
options.D: Article 47

questions.explanation: Article 39(d) directs the State to ensure that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article directs the State to ensure just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?

options.A: Article 42
options.B: Article 39(d)
options.C: Article 46
options.D: Article 47

questions.explanation: Article 42 directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Fundamental Duty promotes renunciation of practices derogatory to the dignity of women?

options.A: Article 51A(e)
options.B: Article 51A(k)
options.C: Article 51A(g)
options.D: Article 51A(a)

questions.explanation: Article 51A(e) makes it a fundamental duty to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which law protects women from domestic violence?

options.A: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
options.B: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
options.C: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
options.D: The Maternity Benefit Act, 1961

questions.explanation: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, provides civil protection and remedies for women facing domestic violence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which law prohibits sexual harassment of women at the workplace?

options.A: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, commonly called the POSH Act
options.B: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
