options.D: Only social pressure

questions.explanation: Causes include patriarchal norms, unequal gender status, the treatment of marriage as a status transaction, son preference, economic expectations, social pressure and the transfer of wealth through marriage practices.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the consequences of dowry?

options.A: Financial hardship, debt, harassment, domestic abuse, forced marriage pressures, violence, dowry deaths, gender discrimination and the devaluation of women
options.B: Only financial hardship
options.C: Only domestic abuse
options.D: Only dowry deaths

questions.explanation: Consequences include financial hardship, debt, harassment, domestic abuse, forced marriage pressures, violence, dowry deaths, gender discrimination and the devaluation of women.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between dowry and gender inequality?

options.A: Dowry reflects and reinforces unequal gender relations when women are treated as financial burdens or when marriage is used to extract wealth from the bride's family
options.B: Dowry promotes gender equality
options.C: Dowry has no relationship with gender inequality
options.D: Dowry only affects economic inequality

questions.explanation: Dowry reflects and reinforces unequal gender relations when women are treated as financial burdens or when marriage is used to extract wealth from the bride's family.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can dowry be prevented?

options.A: Through enforcement of the Dowry Prohibition Act, accessible complaint mechanisms, protection of survivors, gender-equality education, community awareness, responsible marriage practices and social rejection of dowry demands
options.B: Only through legal enforcement
options.C: Only through education
options.D: Only through community awareness

questions.explanation: Prevention requires enforcement of the Dowry Prohibition Act, accessible complaint mechanisms, protection of survivors, gender-equality education, community awareness, responsible marriage practices and social rejection of dowry demands.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is domestic violence under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?

options.A: Abuse or harmful conduct within a domestic relationship, including physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse as defined by the Act
options.B: Only physical abuse within a domestic relationship
options.C: Only economic abuse within a domestic relationship
options.D: Only verbal abuse within a domestic relationship

questions.explanation: Domestic violence is abuse or harmful conduct within a domestic relationship. Under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, it includes physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse as defined by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Act provides civil protection and remedies to women facing domestic violence in India?

options.A: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
options.B: The Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961
options.C: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
options.D: The Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956

questions.explanation: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, provides civil remedies and protection measures for women facing domestic violence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Who can seek relief under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?

options.A: An aggrieved person is a woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and alleges domestic violence, as defined by the Act
options.B: Any person who has experienced violence
options.C: Only a woman who is currently married
options.D: Only a woman who has children

questions.explanation: An aggrieved person is a woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and alleges domestic violence, as defined by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a domestic relationship under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: A relationship between two persons who live or have lived together in a shared household when related by consanguinity, marriage, a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or as family members living together in a joint family, as defined by the Act
options.B: Only a relationship between a husband and wife
options.C: Only a relationship between parents and children
options.D: Only a relationship between siblings

questions.explanation: A domestic relationship is a relationship between two persons who live or have lived together in a shared household when related by consanguinity, marriage, a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or as family members living together in a joint family, as defined by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What types of abuse does the Domestic Violence Act recognise?

options.A: Physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, and economic abuse, subject to the statutory definitions
options.B: Only physical abuse
options.C: Only physical and sexual abuse
options.D: Only verbal and emotional abuse

questions.explanation: The Act recognises physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, and economic abuse, subject to the statutory definitions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is physical abuse under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: Conduct that causes bodily pain, harm or danger to life, limb or health, or impairs health or development, as covered by the Act
options.B: Insults, ridicule and humiliation
options.C: Deprivation of financial resources
options.D: Conduct of a sexual nature that violates dignity

questions.explanation: Physical abuse includes conduct that causes bodily pain, harm or danger to life, limb or health, or impairs health or development, as covered by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is sexual abuse under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: Conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates the dignity of a woman, as covered by the Act
options.B: Conduct that causes bodily pain or harm
options.C: Insults, ridicule and humiliation
options.D: Deprivation of financial resources

questions.explanation: Sexual abuse includes conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates the dignity of a woman, as covered by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is verbal and emotional abuse under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: Insults, ridicule, humiliation, name-calling and other conduct specified in the Act, including certain forms of harassment related to not having a child or a male child
options.B: Conduct that causes bodily pain or harm
options.C: Deprivation of financial resources
options.D: Conduct of a sexual nature that violates dignity

questions.explanation: Verbal and emotional abuse includes insults, ridicule, humiliation, name-calling and other conduct specified in the Act, including certain forms of harassment related to not having a child or a male child.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is economic abuse under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: Deprivation of financial resources, household necessities, maintenance, property or resources to which the aggrieved person is entitled, as well as specified restrictions on access to the shared household and property
options.B: Conduct that causes bodily pain or harm
options.C: Insults, ridicule and humiliation
options.D: Conduct of a sexual nature that violates dignity

questions.explanation: Economic abuse includes deprivation of financial resources, household necessities, maintenance, property or resources to which the aggrieved person is entitled, as well as specified restrictions on access to the shared household and property.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a shared household under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: A household where the aggrieved person lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship, either singly or with the respondent, as defined by the Act
options.B: A household owned jointly by the husband and wife
options.C: A household owned only by the husband
options.D: A household owned only by the wife

questions.explanation: A shared household is a household where the aggrieved person lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship, either singly or with the respondent, as defined by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a Protection Officer under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: An officer appointed by the State Government under the Act to assist the Magistrate and support implementation of the Act's procedures and relief mechanisms
options.B: A police officer who investigates domestic violence cases
options.C: A judicial officer who tries domestic violence cases
options.D: A medical officer who treats domestic violence victims

questions.explanation: A Protection Officer is an officer appointed by the State Government under the Domestic Violence Act to assist the Magistrate and support implementation of the Act's procedures and relief mechanisms.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What reliefs can a Magistrate grant under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: Reliefs may include protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, custody orders, compensation orders and interim or ex parte orders, subject to the Act
options.B: Only protection orders
options.C: Only monetary relief
options.D: Only custody orders

questions.explanation: Reliefs may include protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, custody orders, compensation orders and interim or ex parte orders, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a protection order under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: An order issued by a Magistrate under the Act restraining the respondent from committing specified acts of domestic violence or other prohibited conduct
options.B: An order protecting the aggrieved woman's right to reside in the shared household
options.C: An order granting monetary relief to the aggrieved woman
options.D: An order granting custody of children to the aggrieved woman

questions.explanation: A protection order is an order issued by a Magistrate under the Act restraining the respondent from committing specified acts of domestic violence or other prohibited conduct.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is a residence order under the Domestic Violence Act?

options.A: An order that may protect the aggrieved woman's right to reside in the shared household and may restrain dispossession or direct other measures permitted by the Act
options.B: An order restraining the respondent from committing acts of domestic violence
options.C: An order granting monetary relief to the aggrieved woman
options.D: An order granting custody of children to the aggrieved woman

questions.explanation: A residence order may protect the aggrieved woman's right to reside in the shared household and may restrain dispossession or direct other measures permitted by the Act.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the One Stop Centre scheme in domestic violence cases?

options.A: One Stop Centres facilitate integrated support for women affected by violence, including medical assistance, police facilitation, legal aid, psycho-social counselling and temporary shelter, according to scheme provisions
options.B: One Stop Centres investigate domestic violence cases
options.C: One Stop Centres try domestic violence cases
options.D: One Stop Centres provide pensions to domestic violence victims

questions.explanation: One Stop Centres facilitate integrated support for women affected by violence, including medical assistance, police facilitation, legal aid, psycho-social counselling and temporary shelter, according to scheme provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between domestic violence and dowry harassment?

options.A: Domestic violence is a broader category of abuse within a domestic relationship, while dowry harassment is harassment connected with unlawful dowry demands that may also constitute domestic violence and attract separate criminal or statutory provisions
options.B: Domestic violence applies only to physical abuse, dowry harassment only to economic abuse
options.C: Domestic violence applies only to married women, dowry harassment to all women
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Domestic violence is a broader category of abuse within a domestic relationship. Dowry harassment is harassment connected with unlawful dowry demands; it may also constitute domestic violence and attract separate criminal or statutory provisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which helpline number is commonly used for emergency response in India?
questions.explanation: 112 is India's pan-India emergency response number. Availability of women-specific or local support helplines can vary by State and service.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What should a person do when facing immediate domestic violence danger?

options.A: Move to a safer place if possible and contact emergency services at 112 or local police, a trusted support service or a One Stop Centre; medical care and legal assistance should be sought where needed
options.B: Wait for the violence to stop on its own
options.C: Confront the abuser alone
options.D: Inform neighbours but not the police

questions.explanation: The person should move to a safer place if possible and contact emergency services at 112 or local police, a trusted support service or a One Stop Centre. Medical care and legal assistance should be sought where needed.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is communalism?

options.A: An ideology or political outlook that treats religious communities as separate groups with opposing interests and may promote prejudice, hostility, discrimination or violence between them
options.B: The belief that all religions are equal
options.C: The principle of separation of religion and State
options.D: The practice of religious rituals

questions.explanation: Communalism is an ideology or political outlook that treats religious communities as separate groups with opposing interests and may promote prejudice, hostility, discrimination or violence between them.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major features of communalism?

options.A: Treating religious identity as the primary political identity, stereotyping other communities, portraying community interests as incompatible, spreading distrust and mobilising people through religious divisions
options.B: Promoting interfaith dialogue and harmony
options.C: Treating religious identity as irrelevant to politics
options.D: Portraying all community interests as compatible

questions.explanation: Major features include treating religious identity as the primary political identity, stereotyping other communities, portraying community interests as incompatible, spreading distrust and mobilising people through religious divisions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes of communalism?

options.A: Historical conflicts, political mobilisation, social and economic competition, misinformation, prejudice, segregation, hate speech, institutional failures and the manipulation of religious identity
options.B: Only historical conflicts
options.C: Only political mobilisation
options.D: Only social and economic competition

questions.explanation: Causes may include historical conflicts, political mobilisation, social and economic competition, misinformation, prejudice, segregation, hate speech, institutional failures and the manipulation of religious identity.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is communal violence?

options.A: Violence between or targeting people because of their religious community identity, including attacks on persons, homes, places of worship or property
options.B: Violence within a family
options.C: Violence between political parties
options.D: Violence between castes

questions.explanation: Communal violence is violence between or targeting people because of their religious community identity, including attacks on persons, homes, places of worship or property.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is communal harmony?

options.A: Peaceful coexistence, mutual respect, equal citizenship and cooperation among people belonging to different religious communities
options.B: The dominance of one religious community over others
options.C: The separation of religious communities
options.D: The conversion of all people to one religion

questions.explanation: Communal harmony means peaceful coexistence, mutual respect, equal citizenship and cooperation among people belonging to different religious communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between religion and communalism?

options.A: Religion concerns beliefs, rituals, moral traditions and spiritual practices, while communalism politicises religious identity in a divisive way that may create antagonism or discrimination between communities
options.B: Religion is divisive, communalism is spiritual
options.C: Religion and communalism are identical
options.D: Religion is political, communalism is spiritual

questions.explanation: Religion concerns beliefs, rituals, moral traditions and spiritual practices. Communalism politicises religious identity in a divisive way that may create antagonism or discrimination between communities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is secularism in the Indian constitutional context?

options.A: The State has no official religion and must protect equality and freedom of conscience and religion in accordance with the Constitution
options.B: The State promotes one official religion
options.C: The State bans all religions
options.D: The State treats all religions as equally false

questions.explanation: Indian secularism means that the State has no official religion and must protect equality and freedom of conscience and religion in accordance with the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Articles protect freedom of religion?

options.A: Articles 25 to 28
options.B: Articles 14 to 18
options.C: Articles 19 to 22
options.D: Articles 29 to 30

questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 protect freedom of conscience and religion and regulate related institutional matters.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article guarantees equality before the law?

options.A: Article 14
options.B: Article 15
options.C: Article 25
options.D: Article 29

questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to every person.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion?

options.A: Article 15
options.B: Article 14
options.C: Article 25
options.D: Article 29

questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits the State from discriminating against citizens on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture?

options.A: Article 29
options.B: Article 25
options.C: Article 15
options.D: Article 14

questions.explanation: Article 29 protects the interests of sections of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture and provides protection in relation to admission to specified educational institutions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the National Integration Council?

options.A: It was established as a forum to address issues of national integration and communal harmony and to promote cooperation against divisive forces; its meetings and current activity should be checked from official records
options.B: It is a constitutional body established under Article 263
options.C: It is a statutory body established under the NIA Act
options.D: It is a body established under the RTE Act

questions.explanation: The National Integration Council was established as a forum to address issues of national integration and communal harmony and to promote cooperation against divisive forces. Its meetings and current activity should be checked from official records.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can communalism be prevented?

options.A: Through impartial law enforcement, protection of minorities, civic and constitutional education, responsible public communication, interfaith dialogue, action against incitement and accountability for violence
options.B: Only through law enforcement
options.C: Only through education
options.D: Only through interfaith dialogue

questions.explanation: Prevention requires impartial law enforcement, protection of minorities, civic and constitutional education, responsible public communication, interfaith dialogue, action against incitement and accountability for violence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is hate speech?

options.A: Expression that attacks, threatens or incites discrimination or hostility against people based on characteristics such as religion, caste or ethnicity, with legal treatment depending on specific statutory provisions and facts
options.B: Any criticism of the government
options.C: Any religious preaching
options.D: Any political speech

questions.explanation: Hate speech generally refers to expression that attacks, threatens or incites discrimination or hostility against people based on characteristics such as religion, caste or ethnicity. Its legal treatment depends on the specific statutory provisions and facts.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How does misinformation contribute to communal tension?

options.A: False or misleading claims can spread fear, stereotypes and hostility, especially when circulated rapidly through digital platforms; verification, responsible reporting and timely official communication help reduce this risk
options.B: Misinformation has no effect on communal tension
options.C: Misinformation only affects political campaigns
options.D: Misinformation only affects economic activities

questions.explanation: False or misleading claims can spread fear, stereotypes and hostility, especially when circulated rapidly through digital platforms. Verification, responsible reporting and timely official communication help reduce this risk.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is regionalism?

options.A: A strong identification with a particular region and its interests, often expressed through demands for recognition, development, autonomy, resources or political representation
options.B: A strong identification with a particular religion
options.C: A strong identification with a particular caste
options.D: A strong identification with a particular gender

questions.explanation: Regionalism is a strong identification with a particular region and its interests, often expressed through demands for recognition, development, autonomy, resources or political representation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the positive aspects of regionalism?

options.A: It can promote local culture and language, balanced development, democratic participation, protection of regional interests and demands for fair distribution of resources
options.B: It always leads to violence
options.C: It always challenges national integration
options.D: It always promotes discrimination

questions.explanation: Positive regionalism can promote local culture and language, balanced development, democratic participation, protection of regional interests and demands for fair distribution of resources.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the negative aspects of regionalism?

options.A: It can lead to hostility towards people from other regions, discrimination, exclusion, violence, narrow political mobilisation and challenges to national integration
options.B: It only promotes local culture
options.C: It only promotes balanced development
options.D: It only promotes democratic participation

questions.explanation: Negative regionalism can lead to hostility towards people from other regions, discrimination, exclusion, violence, narrow political mobilisation and challenges to national integration.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes of regionalism?

options.A: Uneven development, linguistic and cultural identities, historical factors, competition over water and other resources, political mobilisation, perceived neglect and demands for autonomy
options.B: Only uneven development
options.C: Only linguistic identities
options.D: Only competition over water

questions.explanation: Causes include uneven development, linguistic and cultural identities, historical factors, competition over water and other resources, political mobilisation, perceived neglect and demands for autonomy.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is regional imbalance?

options.A: Unequal development among regions in income, employment, infrastructure, education, healthcare, investment and public services
options.B: Unequal distribution of population among regions
options.C: Unequal representation of regions in sports
options.D: Unequal distribution of rainfall among regions

questions.explanation: Regional imbalance is unequal development among regions in income, employment, infrastructure, education, healthcare, investment and public services.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is sub-regionalism?

options.A: Identification with or mobilisation around a smaller region within a State or larger region, often based on perceived differences in development, culture or representation
options.B: Identification with a nation as a whole
options.C: Identification with a religion
options.D: Identification with a caste

questions.explanation: Sub-regionalism is identification with or mobilisation around a smaller region within a State or larger region, often based on perceived differences in development, culture or representation.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the relationship between regionalism and federalism?

options.A: Federalism provides constitutional arrangements for sharing power between the Union and States and can accommodate regional diversity and provide democratic channels for addressing regional aspirations and disputes
options.B: Federalism eliminates regionalism entirely
options.C: Regionalism eliminates federalism entirely
options.D: Federalism and regionalism are identical concepts

questions.explanation: Federalism provides constitutional arrangements for sharing power between the Union and States. It can accommodate regional diversity and provide democratic channels for addressing regional aspirations and disputes.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which Article provides for the Inter-State Council?

options.A: Article 263
options.B: Article 280
options.C: Article 246
options.D: Article 338

questions.explanation: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council when it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment, for specified coordination and advisory functions.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the Finance Commission in regional balance?

options.A: The Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280, recommends the distribution of certain tax revenues between the Union and States and among States, helping address fiscal imbalances within the constitutional framework
options.B: The Finance Commission resolves inter-State water disputes
options.C: The Finance Commission reorganises State boundaries
options.D: The Finance Commission conducts the Census

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission, constituted under Article 280, recommends the distribution of certain tax revenues between the Union and States and among States, helping address fiscal imbalances within the constitutional framework.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the role of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?

options.A: It reorganised the boundaries of Indian States and was a major step in linguistic reorganisation after the States Reorganisation Commission's recommendations
options.B: It established the Inter-State Council
options.C: It established the Finance Commission
options.D: It established the National Integration Council

questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956, reorganised the boundaries of Indian States and was a major step in linguistic reorganisation after the States Reorganisation Commission's recommendations.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Who chaired the States Reorganisation Commission?

options.A: Faz Ali, with K. M. Panikkar and H. N. Kunzru as other members
options.B: D. T. Lakdawala
options.C: Suresh D. Tendulkar
options.D: C. Rangarajan

questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Commission was chaired by Faz Ali. Its other members were K. M. Panikkar and H. N. Kunzru.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: How can regional disparities be reduced?

options.A: Through balanced regional planning, infrastructure investment, fair fiscal transfers, decentralisation, public services, employment generation and transparent resource-sharing arrangements
options.B: Only through infrastructure investment
options.C: Only through fair fiscal transfers
options.D: Only through decentralisation

questions.explanation: Balanced regional planning, infrastructure investment, fair fiscal transfers, decentralisation, public services, employment generation and transparent resource-sharing arrangements can reduce disparities.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is drug abuse?

options.A: The harmful or non-medical use of psychoactive substances in ways that can damage physical health, mental health, relationships, education, work or social functioning
options.B: Any use of medicine as prescribed by a doctor
options.C: Any use of alcohol
options.D: Any use of tobacco

questions.explanation: Drug abuse is the harmful or non-medical use of psychoactive substances in ways that can damage physical health, mental health, relationships, education, work or social functioning. Clinical terminology increasingly uses terms such as substance use disorder where appropriate.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is substance dependence?

options.A: A pattern in which a person develops a strong drive to use a substance, may experience difficulty controlling use and may continue despite harmful consequences; clinical diagnosis depends on recognised diagnostic criteria
options.B: Any use of a substance
options.C: Use of a substance in an unsafe way only
options.D: Use of a substance for medical purposes

questions.explanation: Substance dependence is a pattern in which a person develops a strong drive to use a substance, may experience difficulty controlling use and may continue despite harmful consequences. Clinical diagnosis depends on recognised diagnostic criteria.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is substance use disorder?

options.A: A clinically recognised pattern of problematic substance use that causes significant impairment or distress, assessed using diagnostic criteria
options.B: Any use of a substance
options.C: Use of a substance in an unsafe way only
options.D: Use of a substance for medical purposes

questions.explanation: Substance use disorder is a clinically recognised pattern of problematic substance use that causes significant impairment or distress, assessed using diagnostic criteria.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is addiction?

options.A: A commonly used term for a chronic, relapsing pattern of compulsive substance use or behaviour despite harmful consequences; in clinical settings, specific diagnostic terms are preferred
options.B: Any use of a substance
options.C: Use of a substance in an unsafe way only
options.D: Use of a substance for medical purposes

questions.explanation: Addiction is a commonly used term for a chronic, relapsing pattern of compulsive substance use or behaviour despite harmful consequences. In clinical settings, specific diagnostic terms are preferred.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is the difference between drug use, misuse and dependence?

options.A: Drug use means taking a substance; misuse refers to use in an unsafe, inappropriate or non-medical way; dependence describes a pattern involving impaired control and other features; not every use leads to dependence
options.B: Drug use and misuse are identical, dependence is different
options.C: Drug use, misuse and dependence are all identical
options.D: Drug use is always harmful, misuse is always safe

questions.explanation: Drug use means taking a substance; misuse refers to use in an unsafe, inappropriate or non-medical way; dependence describes a pattern involving impaired control and other features. Not every use leads to dependence.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: Which substances are commonly associated with substance-use problems?

options.A: Alcohol, tobacco and nicotine products, opioids, cannabis, sedatives, stimulants, inhalants and certain prescription medicines when used non-medically; legal status and health risks differ by substance
options.B: Only alcohol
options.C: Only tobacco
options.D: Only opioids

questions.explanation: Substances may include alcohol, tobacco and nicotine products, opioids, cannabis, sedatives, stimulants, inhalants and certain prescription medicines when used non-medically. Legal status and health risks differ by substance.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are opioids?

options.A: A class of substances that act on opioid receptors and may be used medically for pain relief; non-medical use can cause dependence and life-threatening respiratory depression
options.B: Substances that increase activity in the central nervous system
options.C: Substances that reduce central nervous system activity
options.D: Volatile substances whose vapours are intentionally inhaled

questions.explanation: Opioids are a class of substances that act on opioid receptors and may be used medically for pain relief. Non-medical use can cause dependence and life-threatening respiratory depression.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are stimulants?

options.A: Substances that increase activity in parts of the central nervous system, with examples including amphetamine-type substances and cocaine; some stimulants also have legitimate medical uses under prescription
options.B: Substances that act on opioid receptors
options.C: Substances that reduce central nervous system activity
options.D: Volatile substances whose vapours are intentionally inhaled

questions.explanation: Stimulants are substances that increase activity in parts of the central nervous system. Examples include amphetamine-type substances and cocaine; some stimulants also have legitimate medical uses under prescription.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are depressants?

options.A: Substances that reduce central nervous system activity, with examples including alcohol, benzodiazepines and some sedative medicines; combining depressants can increase the risk of overdose
options.B: Substances that act on opioid receptors
options.C: Substances that increase central nervous system activity
options.D: Volatile substances whose vapours are intentionally inhaled

questions.explanation: Depressants are substances that reduce central nervous system activity. Examples include alcohol, benzodiazepines and some sedative medicines; combining depressants can increase the risk of overdose.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are inhalants?

options.A: Volatile substances whose vapours are intentionally inhaled to produce psychoactive effects; they can cause serious damage to the brain, heart, lungs, liver and other organs
options.B: Substances that act on opioid receptors
options.C: Substances that increase central nervous system activity
options.D: Substances that reduce central nervous system activity

questions.explanation: Inhalants are volatile substances whose vapours are intentionally inhaled to produce psychoactive effects. They can cause serious damage to the brain, heart, lungs, liver and other organs.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the major causes and risk factors for drug abuse?

options.A: Peer pressure, stress, trauma, family difficulties, availability of substances, social exclusion, mental-health problems, lack of support and exposure to substance use; no single factor explains every case
options.B: Only peer pressure
options.C: Only stress
options.D: Only availability of substances

questions.explanation: Risk factors may include peer pressure, stress, trauma, family difficulties, availability of substances, social exclusion, mental-health problems, lack of support and exposure to substance use. No single factor explains every case.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What are the consequences of drug abuse?

options.A: Dependence, overdose, injury, mental and physical illness, family conflict, educational or employment disruption, financial hardship, unsafe behaviour and legal problems
options.B: Only dependence
options.C: Only mental and physical illness
options.D: Only legal problems

questions.explanation: Consequences may include dependence, overdose, injury, mental and physical illness, family conflict, educational or employment disruption, financial hardship, unsafe behaviour and legal problems.

questions.subject: Indian Society
questions.question: What is overdose?

options.A: A situation in which a person takes a toxic amount of a substance, causing potentially life-threatening effects such as unconsciousness, seizures, breathing problems or cardiac complications
options.B: A situation in which a person takes a prescribed dose of medicine
options.C: A situation in which a person takes a substance for the first time
